tex_content.html:
If $x\in \Omega $ is the center of strong $\epsilon $-necks at times $t_n\to T$, then $(x,T)$ is the center of a strong $2\epsilon $-neck. \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch Rescale so $R(x,T)=1$. On $B(x,T,2\epsilon ^{-1}/3)$ the neck flow lines exist on $(T-1,T]$ and the rescaled neck metrics converge smoothly. Restricting the neck coordinates to $S^2\times (-\epsilon ^{-1}/2,\epsilon ^{-1}/2)$ gives a strong $2\epsilon $-neck at time $T$.

□
